name: Integrated Design Projectweek
description:
The ecological and climate crisis we face today demands that we think and work differently and, in particular, that we teach and learn differently. We cannot solve these issues alone and have to learn not only the processes but also the language by which to communicate with other disciplines. To be productive, interdisciplinary work requires that we develop the necessary skills to be open-minded, engage others, and be willing to think critically of our own approaches. These skills are often taken for granted. However, our experience in practice and in teaching the past semesters has shown that true innovation only comes about when each party has a basic understanding and common language with the others and can engage in a line of questioning that leads to productive rethinking.

The “Spatial Systems” Project Week will allow students in the BA-3 course to conduct a focused, in-depth investigation into the integration of structural engineering and climate-responsive design to drive the concept and expressive elements of a building. Through a combination of lectures, hands-on workshops, model-based design experiments, and real-world environmental measurements, students will test theoretical concepts directly against observed spatial conditions. Taking their semester project as a reference, students will design and build a large-scale physical model during the week that will explore the following:
1. The role of structural engineering in shaping the experience and atmosphere of the space through exposed structures.
2. The integration of daylight into the space by natural means.
3. The integration of natural ventilation and passive heating/cooling measures, together with the structural and spatial design.
4. The relationship of these technical measures as architectural opportunities in designing the spatial the functional relationships in a building.

The Project Week format would allow for an intensive immersion in the three disciplines and give the students a specific goal and product to test these ideas.
The students will be asked to produce the following:
1. A larger-scale model that captures a cross-section of the building (1:20/1:50)
2. A documentation of the development process, focusing particularly on the analysis of daylight, airflow, structures, and how they affect design decisions
3. A documentation of the final result
